title: a transform wrote twice the lowpass width into a plane that was narrower
consumer: libavcodec/cfhd.c, the transform-2 path writing into the plane buffer
object: the plane's pixel buffer, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: an inverse transform doubles the width and writes past a narrower plane
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation per plane, no inner layer.
fidelity: model consumer, real guard: the pin's added term is `lowpass_width * 2 > s->plane[plane].width`, and the case asserts exactly that inequality.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/cfhd.c carries the added term `|| lowpass_width * 2 > s->plane[plane].width` in both transform-2 guards. The pre-fix form, ending at `lowpass_height < 3`, is at 16b2049d4d^.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **CAUGHT.** signal=34, si_code=1 (the BOUNDS code), fault at 0x1021f6, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_write_probe_u8 0x1021de` from the ELF independently of the run -- the fault lies inside the probe's extent, the offset being the -O0 frame setup, and the RANGE is the attribution criterion rather than equality with the symbol address. The crossing leaves the allocator's USABLE size, which is what malloc bounds the capability to, so there is no size-class slack for it to hide in. tools/size-class-audit.py predicted this reading from the measured request size alone, and the two agree.
cheribsd-revocation.platform: stock CheriBSD purecap, kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, revocation ON (--runtime-revocation on); both platform controls cheribsd-abi and cheribsd-bounds PASSED in the same boot.

native-detect.oracle: the buggy arm's access crosses the allocation and the case's damage flag is set; the fixed arm's bound keeps it inside. The arms differ by the upstream fix, not by protection. nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner allocator between, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the crossing length is a MULTIPLE of a stream-declared value rather than the value itself -- the transform doubles it -- so a guard on the declared width alone does not bound the write.
